memory_update.text: MPWR should remain the reference benchmark for AI rack point-of-load and module-level power exposure; not underfollowed, but useful for comparing smaller power-conversion names.

NVTS is a high-optionality GaN/SiC AI rack power candidate with explicit NVIDIA 800V collaboration evidence, but should be treated as speculative until production purchase orders and revenue ramps are visible.
POWI is a lower-attention mid-cap candidate for 800VDC AI data-center power via high-voltage PowiGaN; verify official NVIDIA/OCP certification and materiality.
VICR has technically relevant 800V-to-48V conversion capability, but AI data-center production adoption remains the key evidence gap.

AEIS appears relevant as a rack power-supply and possible 800V DC-DC platform supplier; include in a follow-up pass if primary company announcement or filing confirms the recent 800V AI platform details.

Add MPWR as the high-attention reference benchmark for AI rack point-of-load and high-current power modules; use it to compare smaller module suppliers rather than as the main underfollowed alpha target.

Add VICR as an underfollowed pure-play power-module candidate tied to 48V direct-to-PoL, vertical power delivery, and AI accelerator current-delivery constraints; key survival test is production adoption and backlog tied to AI platforms.
Add NVTS as a speculative-shadow GaN/SiC optionality candidate for 800VDC AI factory architectures; require production orders and revenue conversion before upgrading confidence.

Add BELFB as a lower-attention data-center rack power and connectivity supplier with possible second-order exposure through AC/DC-HVDC shelves, DC/DC modules, OCP rack power, magnetics, and custom power modules.

Power Integrations, onsemi, Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, Infineon OTC ADR, Delta, Lite-On, Flex, and ABB appear in the 800VDC ecosystem but were not included due to the four-candidate cap; later passes should map them by exchange listing, purity, and market-cap fit.

The central chokepoint is not only facility power availability; it is the staged conversion path from AC/grid or HVDC distribution to 800VDC, intermediate bus, 48V or lower rails, and ultimately sub-1V processor core delivery.
VICR is a node-specific reference asset for AI/HPC point-of-load and 48V power-module architectures, but its current market cap places it outside the preferred small/mid-cap discovery range.

NVTS is a high-optionality GaN/SiC discovery candidate for NVIDIA-style 800 VDC AI-factory power, but survival in later layers requires proof of production purchase orders and data-center revenue ramp.
POWI is an underfollowed high-voltage GaN/power-IC candidate with explicit NVIDIA Kyber 800 VDC reference-design evidence; verify production conversion and revenue materiality.
AOSL is a smaller power-semiconductor candidate with SiC/GaN 800 VDC positioning; classify as hypothesis until named customers, production sockets, and revenue contribution are verified.

BELFB/Bel Fuse appeared in discovery as a lower-attention data-center power-supply and connectivity vendor with 48V/front-end power products, but it was excluded due to the four-candidate limit and should be revisited in a later power-shelf/distribution pass.

For AI rack power conversion, later layers should separate sockets by stage: grid/MVAC-to-800V conversion, 800V-to-48/54V shelf or sidecar conversion, 48V-to-intermediate bus, and point-of-load/sub-1V delivery.
MPWR should remain a reference candidate for point-of-load AI rack power, but later layers need primary evidence for customer/platform exposure rather than relying on market narrative.
VICR is an underfollowed power-module candidate tied to 48V/direct-to-load architectures; survival depends on evidence of volume conversion into AI accelerator systems.

NVTS has the most explicit NVIDIA/800V public linkage among the smaller power-semiconductor candidates, but it carries high evidence and timing risk until production orders and revenue contribution are visible.
POWI is a low-attention second-order candidate for 800V AI data-center GaN auxiliary/conversion supplies; classify as hypothesis until design wins or production revenue are confirmed.

The node appears to be shifting from generic data-center power equipment toward an architecture-specific semiconductor/module map: 800V HVDC distribution, GaN/SiC high-voltage conversion, intermediate bus conversion, and point-of-load regulation.

Need a follow-up pass for non-U.S. or OTC-listed reference suppliers such as Infineon, ABB, Schneider-like peers, and possibly EPC/private suppliers to understand competitive pressure on US-listed names.

node: AI rack power conversion from grid input to point-of-load
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for AI rack power conversion with a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: Monolithic Power Systems as the high-attention point-of-load/module leader tied to AI data-center power solutions. Underfollowed/discovery lane: Vicor, Navitas, and Power Integrations as narrower power-conversion or GaN/SiC specialists with credible 800V or high-voltage AI-rack relevance, but differing evidence quality. Key chokepoint logic: NVIDIA-backed 800VDC architectures shift value toward suppliers that can convert efficiently from facility/rack-level high voltage down to intermediate and chip-proximate rails. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Layer 1B expansion for AI rack power conversion finds a small set of US-listed power-conversion names with plausible exposure to the shift from legacy 48/54V rack distribution toward higher-voltage 800VDC architectures and denser point-of-load delivery. Reference context remains NVIDIA's 800VDC ecosystem and larger analog/power suppliers, but this pass prioritizes less-obvious component/module vendors: Vicor for high-density modular power and vertical/point-of-load delivery, Navitas for GaN/SiC optionality in 800VDC AI factories, Bel Fuse for AC/DC and DC/DC rack power supplies, and Monolithic Power Systems as a higher-attention reference for cloud/HPC point-of-load power modules. None of these are buy/sell recommendations; weaker claims require revenue, design-win, customer, and volume-ramp verification.
